newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-HASEK SHUTS OUT LISTLESS BRUINS IN BUFFALO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-HASEK SHUTS OUT LISTLESS BRUINS IN BUFFALO VICTORY.

text.p: Dominik Hasek recorded his fourth shutout of the season and Michal Grosek scored twice to lead the Buffalo Sabres to a 4-0 victory Saturday over the Boston Bruins, who went winless on a five-game homestand.
Hasek made 29 saves, stopping Andre Roy on a pair of breakaways to record his 19th career shutout.
Donald Audette added a power-play goal and an assist for Buffalo (15-14-2), who have back-to-back wins at Boston.

"The Bruins are playing like they don't want it right now. I don't know what's going on with Boston," said Sabres' Brian Holzinger. "I can't understand why they're playing the way they are. They have some good players, we just outhustled them."
The Bruins (10-14-5), who went 0-4-1 on their homestand, lost right wing Sandy Moger, defenceman Ray Bourque and centre Clayton Beddoes to injuries.
"Certainly we'll never stop trying," added Bruins coach Steve Kasper. "(It's) no secret we're not playing well right now. I don't have the answer for you right now."
Audette scored the only goal Hasek needed during a two-man advantage at 3:12 of the first period. Grosek scored twice in the third period to give Buffalo breathing room.

In Los Angeles, Philippe Boucher and Brad Smyth scored in the final 89 seconds after Los Angeles pulled its goaltender for an extra attacker as the Kings rallied for a 4-4 tie with the Washington Capitals, winless in their last six games.

Los Angeles yanked goalie Byron Dafoe for an extra skater with 2:29 remaining and it paid off exactly one minute later when Boucher whipped a one-timer from the edge of the right faceoff circle that beat Olaf Kolzig to the stick side.

Dafoe went to the bench again with 50 seconds remaining and Smyth tied it 24 seconds later with his second goal of the game. Kolzig stopped two shots by Rob Blake, but Smyth poked a loose puck into the net before Kolzig could smother it.
In Hartford, Garth Snow made 21 saves for his first career shutout and Rod Brind'Amour scored twice as the Philadelphia Flyers completed a home-and-home sweep of the Hartford Whalers with a 4-0 win.
John LeClair had a goal and an assist in the first period as Philadelphia extended its unbeaten streak to seven (6-0-1) and improved to 13-2-1 in its last 16 meetings with Hartford.
Snow, starting in place of Ron Hextall, made five saves in the first period and eight in each of the final two periods.
"I think we really played well for 60 minutes," said Snow. "I did not really have to make any big saves."
At New Jersey, Darcy Tucker scored a power-play goal on a deflection with 2:33 left in the second period to rally the Montreal Canadiens into a 3-3 tie with the New Jersey Devils.
Brian Savage set up all three goals for Montreal, who have just two wins in their last 12 trips to the Meadowlands.
The Devils are 4-1-1 in their last six games.
Brodeur made 18 saves and Jocelyn Thibault picked up the tie in relief of Pat Jablonski, stopping 29 of 30 shots.

At Tampa, Chris Gratton scored twice and Shawn Burr and Alexander Selivanov tallied 51 seconds apart early in the third period to lift the Tampa Bay Lightning to a 4-1 win over the New York Islanders.
Tampa Bay extended its unbeaten streak to four games (3-0-1) in ending the Isles' three-game winning streak.
"It is nice to get rewarded finally," said Gratton. "The effort and heart have been there and the puck finally has started to bounce our way."
In Toronto, Keith Tkachuk scored twice and Cliff Ronning added a goal and an assist as the Phoenix Coyotes handed the Toronto Maple Leafs their league-leading 19th loss, 5-3.
Dave Manson and Jeremy Roenick had the other goals for the Coyotes, who are 2-0 since general manager John Paddock was fired and have won six of their last nine games overall.
Darcy Wakaluk stopped 30 shots for Phoenix. Felix Potvin made 35 saves, but lost for the seventh time in eight starts.

In Calgary, Dave Gagner and Theo Fleury each had a goal and an assist during a three-goal second period and rookie Dwayne Roloson made 24 saves as the Calgary Flames surprised the Colorado Avalanche 4-1.
After a stretch that saw Calgary score only 12 times in nine games, the Flames have 14 goals during a three-game unbeaten streak (2-0-1).

"Tonight, we did everything we had to do to win," said Roloson, whose club improved to 12-16-4. "Offensively, we got a couple of breaks and that just sort of jump-started our team and from then on, we did the perfect game."
The loss dropped Colorado to 18-9-4.
